what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer: the commands the person's AI runs on the person's own computer to read, add or take out Trillion's hooks in an AI app there, and to read, preview, add or take out that app's Trillion MCP entry. The hooks and helpers themselves are started by harness/setup.mjs and are not rows.

payload.label: Set up an AI harness on a computer
payload.job: Inspect, apply or remove the account's hooks for one chosen AI harness on an exact owned computer
payload.description: Runs the shared signed-app harness installer on the exact recorded computer. Inspect is observational; apply and remove require authorization. Preserves other settings, disabled hooks, managed policies, models and permissions. A configured hook is not evidence of execution. Codex trust requires explicit review of all current definition hashes and refuses changed definitions before writing. Returns the original typed report with computer attribution. Requires the installed computer host to advertise this tool and its exact computer scope; old or offline hosts remain unavailable. No shell, arbitrary module, download, model launch or personal-file import can be selected. After apply, run inspect again to obtain current evidence.

trust_hooks.description: Only true for an explicitly authorized Codex apply after reviewing the exact current definitions.

reviewed_definition_hashes.description: All current configuration.evidence.hooks definition_hash values from the reviewed inspect report; required only when trust_hooks is true.

payload.label: Set up Trillion's hooks in an AI app on this computer
payload.job: Read, add or take out the hooks that keep an AI app's sessions on this computer as the person's records (Claude Code or Codex)
payload.description: Runs harness/setup.mjs with --action inspect, apply or remove for one AI app on this computer (claude-code or codex). inspect writes nothing and answers a report: status, ready, checks (each with id, status and reason), changes it would make and boundaries (what this installer never does: write an MCP entry, open a browser, grant notification permission). apply writes the hooks named in harness/setup.json into that app's own settings, keeping the person's existing settings and permission choices; remove takes them out again. The full hook suite needs the Trillion Mac app and macOS Keychain: on another platform the platform check answers unsupported and nothing is written. Exit 0 means ready, 2 means not ready (the checks say why), 1 means the request was wrong (standard error says what to change).

action.description: inspect reads only; apply and remove change the app's settings and are run only when the person asks.

harness.description: The AI app on this computer.

get_it: npm ci, from the root of the checkout
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Run inspect first and tell the person what is ready and what each failed check says. Run apply or remove only when the person asks for that change, and tell them what changed. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: The AI session harness moved here from Trillion-X/trillion (moved-from.json): harness/setup.mjs and harness/setup.json

payload.label: Connect an AI app on this computer to Trillion
payload.job: Read, preview, add or take out the Trillion MCP entry in AI apps on this computer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor)
payload.description: Runs harness/setup.mjs with --action mcp-inspect, mcp-preview, mcp-register or mcp-unregister for the AI apps named in client (a comma-separated list of claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, cursor). mcp-inspect and mcp-preview write nothing: they answer each app's config file path, whether a Trillion entry is there now, and a review_hash for the exact change. mcp-register writes the entry only when given that review_hash as reviewed, so the person sees the change before it is made; mcp-unregister takes it out. Claude Code and Codex use the bridge the Trillion Mac app installs, which keeps the account key in Keychain; an entry here does not by itself sign the app in (each result's sign_in says how). Exit 0 means every app was handled, 2 means one was blocked or has a custom entry, 1 means the request was wrong (standard error says what to change).

action.description: mcp-inspect and mcp-preview read only; mcp-register and mcp-unregister change the apps' config and are run only when the person asks.

reviewed.description: For mcp-register: the review_hash mcp-preview answered, after the person has seen the change.

get_it: npm ci, from the root of the checkout
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Run mcp-preview, show the person each app's change, and only when they say yes run mcp-register with `--reviewed` and that review_hash added at the end of `run`. Then tell them each result's sign_in step. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: The AI session harness moved here from Trillion-X/trillion (moved-from.json): harness/setup.mjs and harness/mcp-registration.mjs

payload.label: Start a Codex run on this computer
payload.job: Start one fresh Codex run in a folder on this computer and get its run id (harness/codex-runs.mjs startCodexRun)
payload.description: Starts `codex exec` detached in the given folder, with the prompt read from the message file (never on the command line). Answers the run id and state running. Read the run with tool:read-a-codex-run-on-this-computer; end it with tool:cancel-a-codex-run-on-this-computer. Codex uses the person's own login; nothing here reads a credential.

folder.description: The folder Codex runs in. Must exist on this computer.

message_file.description: A plain text file holding the prompt. Must not be empty.

get_it: npm ci, from the root of the checkout
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Tell the person the run id; read it with the read row and cancel it with the cancel row only when the person asks.

provenance.source: Landed as harness/codex-runs.mjs (commit 597ed7061) and its CLI entry point in this lane

payload.label: Read a Codex run on this computer
payload.job: Read a Codex run's output after a byte position and its state (harness/codex-runs.mjs readCodexRun)
payload.description: Answers the run's state (running, exited with exit_code, ended or cancelled), the output bytes after the given position (whole UTF-8 characters only), and next, the position to read from next time. Refuses a run id that is not a codex run.

after.description: The byte position to read after; 0 for the start.

get_it: npm ci, from the root of the checkout
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Read from next each time; stop reading once the state is not running.

provenance.source: Landed as harness/codex-runs.mjs (commit 597ed7061) and its CLI entry point in this lane

payload.label: Cancel a Codex run on this computer
payload.job: End a running Codex run's process group and read back that it is cancelled (harness/codex-runs.mjs cancelCodexRun)
payload.description: Ends the run only while it is still the same running process (its start time is checked). Answers the state and cancelled true when it was running; a run that is not running answers cancelled false.

get_it: npm ci, from the root of the checkout
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Run it only when the person asks to stop the run.

provenance.source: Landed as harness/codex-runs.mjs (commit 597ed7061) and its CLI entry point in this lane

payload.label: Manage signed-in Claude Cloud sessions
payload.job: Find Claude Cloud agents across the accounts signed in on my computer or server, read their work, resume one existing session or start an explicitly named new one
payload.description: Uses only the Claude Code accounts already signed in on the computer where this operation executes. With accounts, lists config folders without reading secrets. With list, returns recent cloud sessions. With read, summarizes one exact session including its task, last answers, PRs, pushes and questions. With resume, sends one continuation message to one existing session; it does not launch a replacement. With start, explicitly makes one new cloud session for named repositories. A dry run makes no changes. No access token is ever returned, copied or sent to Trillion.

config_folder.description: Claude Code config folder directly under the authenticated computer account home; find names with accounts first.

session_id.description: Exact existing cloud-session ID for read or resume.

limit.description: Most sessions returned per account for list, 100 by default.

repositories.description: Comma-separated GitHub owner/repo names, only for a deliberate new session.

message.description: Continuation instructions, kept in memory only by the session control; required for resume or start.

dry_run.description: With resume or start, return the operation without sending it.

output_schema.description: Accounts, sessions, one session with work summary, or a receipt containing the cloud session ID and sent event. No credentials.

provenance.source: harness/read-cloud-sessions.mjs and harness/claude-cloud-control.mjs; existing authenticated Claude Code accounts only

payload.label: Take the tasks given to this computer's AI, kept running by the engine
payload.job: Keep this computer's task taker running inside the person's own engine: it takes each task given to this computer's AI (its assignees name this computer's taker), runs the AI the person chose on it headless, checks the result file the AI writes and finishes the task, or gives it back with the reason. Switching its wake on is the one yes; no launchd job, login item or hand-started process is needed.
payload.description: Runs harness/take-open-work-in-a-run.mjs as a kept-open session of invoke kind computer: HOME is the run's kept folder, the settings in the input are written as this computer's take-open-work.computer.json, and the helper's handler (wake-handlers/take-open-work.mjs) passes over the given tasks now, every full_pass_every_minutes, and as soon as a run it started ends. The tasks are rows of the database `settings.tasks_store` names, reached only through the run's door with the four task tools its records right names (run-sql-in-my-database, take-a-task, change-a-task, finish-a-task). The AI is the program of the run's start-a-program grant (program_kind ai-developer: it may change files only in its settings folder, the one work folder granted, the person's own settings folders and the temporary folders, and reaches the network only through the run's proxy). A Claude login is the vault value `claude_token_name`, mounted only in the run's environment as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, so the run reaches only the hosts that value may go to. `settings.computer_name` keeps the taker's agent id, and so its users row, the same as when it ran by hand. Its AI runs get no account connection: the task prompt has them write the result file, and the taker finishes the task itself.

settings.description: This computer's take-open-work.computer.json values, overlaid on harness/take-open-work.json: computer_name, chosen_ai, then_ai, tasks_store, account ({credential: {from: "run door", fd: 3}}), work_mcp (null: AI runs get no account connection), ais (each command's program as {granted_program}), working_folder ({granted_work} or {kept_home}). {granted_program}, {granted_work} and {kept_home} stand for the grant's program and work folder and the run's kept folder.

computer.description: The grant the person gives this run (computer.start-a-program), with exactly these keys

program.description: The AI program the taker starts, as installed on this computer (a link its updater moves is followed at each start)

settings.description: The folder the AI program keeps its settings in

work.description: The one folder the AI may change files in, such as the folder that holds the person's code

claude_token_name.description: The vault name of the Claude login the AI runs use, mounted only in the run's environment as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN

output_schema.description: A kept-open session answers no result: each pass writes one JSON line to its output (what was taken, started, finished or given back).

provenance.source: harness/take-open-work.mjs and wake-handlers/take-open-work.mjs, the taker the helper (harness/wake-sessions.mjs) runs on a computer made from its row, started here by the engine instead of a service manager
